description: Judges a claimed accuracy or related rate against the supplied counts and returns the kit's verdict, reasons and suggested statement. It takes the caller's word on who labeled the items and how they were sampled. It cannot determine whether the system is accurate, the labels are right or the sample represents production. For a random sample with human labels and 990 of 1,000 correct, an accuracy claim of '98%' is supported and '99.5%' is contradicted.

benchmark.description: The named set for complete or held-out-split sampling.

display.description: Printed form of the claim's figure.

metric.description: Claimed metric. The kit returns a refusal for recognized metrics it cannot assess.

text.description: Claim wording. Required to name the benchmark for fixed-set claims.

value.description: Claimed rate as a proportion from 0 to 1.

options.description: Optional assessment policy. Omit to use the kit defaults.

conservative.description: Require support at the conservative end of the interval.

maxAgeDays.description: Maximum age of the evaluation. Requires now.

minN.description: Minimum sample size for an interval-based verdict. Default 30.

requireScope.description: Refuse a claim with no declared population.

strictPrecision.description: Treat excessive printed precision as an overstatement.

population.description: Identifiers for the population claimed and the population evaluated.

raters.description: Number of independent human raters, if known.

source.description: Declared label source. Automated means deterministic known answers.

retractions.description: Known retractions and whether the sample included them.

sample.description: Counts. Omit if they were not disclosed.

correct.description: Number of correct items. Supply correct, errors, or both.

errors.description: Number of errors. If both counts are given, they must sum to n.

n.description: Number of items in the denominator.

strata.description: Required for stratified samples. Counts must add up to the sample.
